sn22.8:1.2: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you agitation through clinging and nonagitation through nonclinging.
sn22.8:1.3: Listen to that and attend closely….
sn22.8:1.4: “And how, bhikkhus, is there agitation through clinging?
sn22.8:1.5: Here, bhikkhus, the uninstructed worldling regards form thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’
sn22.8:1.6: That form of his changes and alters. With the change and alteration of form,
sn22.8:1.7: there arise in him sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair.
sn22.8:1.11: consciousness thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’
sn22.8:1.12: That consciousness of his changes and alters. With the change and alteration of consciousness,
sn22.8:1.13: there arise in him sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair.
sn22.8:1.14: “It is in such a way, bhikkhus, that there is agitation through clinging.
sn22.8:2.1: “And how, bhikkhus, is there nonagitation through nonclinging?
sn22.8:2.2: Here, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple does not regard form thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’
sn22.8:2.3: That form of his changes and alters. With the change and alteration of form,
sn22.8:2.4: there do not arise in him sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair.
sn22.8:2.8: consciousness thus: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self.’
sn22.8:2.9: That consciousness of his changes and alters. With the change and alteration of consciousness,
sn22.8:2.10: there do not arise in him sorrow, lamentation, pain, displeasure, and despair.
sn22.8:2.11: “It is in such a way, bhikkhus, that there is nonagitation through nonclinging.”
